item.title: Enquiry Number: 22125311, 13th October
item.description:
As I have done for the past several years, I recently submitted a request for the height of the hedgerow backing onto my garden to be reduced to the same height as in previous years. I specifically asked for this to be done the next time the hedges were being cut. Today, I received an email informing me that someone had inspected the hedge and that “It does not currently meet our criteria for an urgent repair but we will monitor the issue in our routine inspections.” I think there may have been a misunderstanding. I did not request an urgent repair. I made a request for routine maintenance, as I have done on several occasions in the past. On each occasion, the top of the hedge has been cut back when the sides are being trimmed. My last request was made in February 2024, and the hedge was subsequently cut back in January 2025. I am therefore asking for the same work to be carried out as part of the next routine hedge-cutting visit to this road. Could you also clarify whether there is a policy or responsibility to keep the height of this hedgerow to two metres, to prevent residents’ gardens from losing light? The height has been reduced on numerous occasions in response to previous requests, so I would appreciate an explanation if the approach has now changed. I would be grateful if you could confirm that my request has been recorded as one for routine maintenance, rather than an urgent repair, and advise when the hedge is next scheduled to be cut.
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): The Poplars, Hatherley, Cheltenham, Cheltenham
